chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it regarding
a boy who entered the house of a people, so he fell into the well. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they were suspicious, they would be responsible.'

key_terms.ضَمِنُوا: They became liable/responsible (financially or for compensation)
key_terms.مُتَّهَمِينَ: Suspicious; expected to be careful or liable due to negligence or duty of care

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a homeowner to be liable if a child falls into their well?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from *Al-Kafi* articulates the principle of *daman* (financial liability) based on the presumption of fault (*istishab al-daman*) when a child enters a dwelling. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that inhabitants are liable for damages unless they can prove they exercised due diligence, reflecting the broader legal maxim that the burden of proof lies with the defendant in cases of suspected negligence.
